answer: A per-identity bond of real value must be locked before an agent can mine, with a slow cooldown keeping that capital tied up long after withdrawal. To run a thousand sybils an attacker must post a thousand separate bonds and fund them at once, so identity stops being free and becomes a large illiquid cost. Every miner also races the epoch puzzle, and each solution passes through a scoring kernel that ranks submissions separately, so the attacker pays fresh compute per clone instead of sharing one comet-like forged proof or a single sonnet of reused answers.
